sn55.26:1.2: The sick Anāthapiṇḍika was also consoled by Ānanda at [sn55.27:3.2](). At [mn143](), Sāriputta consoles him in his final hours. In other cases, we find the Buddha making such visits to sick monks ([sn22.87:2.7](), [sn22.88:2.8](), [sn46.14:2.1](), [sn46.15:2.1](), [an6.56:2.1]()), but for some reason visits to householders are only attested for Sāriputta ([mn97:28.2]()) or Ānanda ([sn47.29:2.2]()).
sn55.26:18.3: Right knowledge and right freedom are normally only qualities of an arahant, but here they are ascribed to Anāthapiṇḍika though he is only a stream-enterer. See note on [sn45.26:2.2]().
